title: Slingshot
teaches: The Slingshot as we trade it: a leader that just had a drive pulls back a few closes under the 4-day EMA of the highs, orderly and shallow, and the buy is the first decisive close back over that line, never the gap day and never the guess at the low; the stop sits a few cents under the trigger day's low, a third comes off at 3R and 5R with the rest on the trail, and a loss taken at the stop is the system working.

facts.quote: This setup is to target a reversal of a shallow pull back.
facts.claim: Scot1and: the setup targets the reversal of a shallow pullback.

facts.quote: The theory behind this setup is that we take a powerful stock and stretch it with pull back.  Then when momentum resumes we enter.
facts.claim: Scot1and: take a powerful stock, let a pullback stretch it, and enter when momentum resumes.

facts.quote: The resumption of the momentum for the slingshot is triggered by the break of the 4EMA of the HIGHS.
facts.claim: Scot1and: the trigger is the break of the 4-period EMA of the highs.

facts.quote: Power can be found using a variety of scans.  52 Week high, RSI, High OBV, high Mdt.  High RS compared to the S&P.
facts.claim: Scot1and finds power with strength scans, including high relative strength against the S&P.

facts.quote: After the Slingshot shoots, the EMA 4 should never be breached on a close.  Consider it the trailing stop on the position.
facts.claim: Scot1and's own trail: a close under the EMA 4; not ours.

facts.quote: My Slingshot indicator is simply a 4EMA of the highs.
facts.claim: Scot1and's write-up: the indicator is a 4EMA of the highs.

facts.quote: First, there must be upward momentum. A pull back in a stock in a downtrend is merely an opportunity to sell into strength.
facts.claim: Scot1and: upward momentum first; a pullback in a downtrend is a chance to sell, not to buy.

facts.quote: Tight trading ranges before the trigger are ideal for two reasons. It signals that the selling pressure is waning and perhaps, more importantly, it permits very tight stops.
facts.claim: Scot1and: tight ranges before the trigger show selling pressure fading and allow very tight stops.

facts.quote: I typically place my stop at the low of the slingshot day. Or at most, the bottom of the consolidation period. Stops should be tight, much tighter than a breakout.
facts.claim: Scot1and: the stop is the low of the slingshot day, or at most the bottom of the consolidation.

facts.quote: Ideally, we want to find a stock that has recently made a strong move.
facts.claim: Scot1and: find a stock that has recently made a strong move.

facts.quote: The advantage of the setup is that it provides a low risk entry with a tight stop.
facts.claim: Scot1and: the setup's advantage is a low-risk entry with a tight stop.

facts.quote: The Slingshot setup, developed by Scot1and, is a strategy designed to capitalize on entering powerful stocks immediately after a pullback.
facts.claim: Deepvue: Scot1and's Slingshot enters powerful stocks right after a pullback.

facts.quote: This setup is characterized by the price crossing above the high of the 5-day Exponential Moving Average (EMA) from the period under analysis.
facts.claim: Deepvue describes a 5-day EMA; a dissent from the originator's 4.

facts.quote: The stop loss is at the low of the slingshot indicator trigger bar, so we want consolidation as it lowers the amount of risk on the trade.
facts.claim: Analyzing Alpha: the stop is the low of the trigger bar, so a tight consolidation lowers the risk.

facts.quote: The slingshot indicator, which is a component of the slingshot setup, fires when the current bar’s close crosses the 4-ema of the highs.
facts.claim: Analyzing Alpha: the indicator fires when the close crosses the 4-period EMA of the highs.

facts.quote: Scot1and developed the slingshot setup to get into a powerful stock after a pullback just as the downward momentum stops and the stock begins to go back up.
facts.claim: Analyzing Alpha: the Slingshot gets into a powerful stock after a pullback, as the downward momentum stops.

facts.quote: That logically makes our stop the low of entry day.
facts.claim: Bonde: the stop is the low of the entry day.

facts.quote: Stop first (by default a few cents under the day's low or the prior day's low, F62); the size comes from the stop; if the honest stop does not fit the risk, skip the trade.
facts.claim: A3: stop first; the size comes from the stop; if the honest stop does not fit, skip.

facts.quote: The stop is the exit. It only moves up, never down or wider. The one exception is the gap rule (B20).
facts.claim: A4: the stop is the exit; it only moves up; the gap rule is the one exception.

facts.quote: Shares = account × risk % ÷ (entry − stop), rounded down, then capped: the size is the SMALLER of the risk-based size and the position cap
facts.claim: A5: shares are account times risk percent, divided by entry minus stop, rounded down, then capped.

facts.quote: The full size at one price with one stop; no adding.
facts.claim: A5: full size at one price with one stop; no adding.

facts.quote: "I almost never take a loss greater than 3%": the stop usually sits within about 3% of the buy (a loss on the position, not the account).
facts.claim: A13: the stop usually sits within about 3% of the buy.

facts.quote: Move the stop to breakeven at 2R to 5R, ideally. The first trim: the hard rule is a third at 3R; ideally anywhere from 3R to 6R, and in practice he mostly waits for 5R.
facts.claim: B19: breakeven between 2R and 5R; the hard rule for the first trim is a third at 3R.

facts.quote: A gap against the stop: the first 30 minutes of the gap-down day decide. The low of the first 30-minute bar is the new stop.
facts.claim: B20: on a gap through the stop, the first 30-minute low is the new stop.

facts.quote: With a ceiling: if the first 30 minutes take the loss past 2R, get out.
facts.claim: B20's ceiling: past 2R in the first 30 minutes, get out.

facts.quote: No new buys in the 3 days before an earnings report; hold through a report only if the trade is up 5R.
facts.claim: B22: no new buys in the 3 days before a report; hold through one only if up 5R.

facts.quote: Trade only stocks at $10 or more that trade at least $20 million a day.
facts.claim: B23: only stocks at $10 or more trading at least $20 million a day.

facts.quote: The 200-day line: no longs below the 200-day simple moving average, unless it is a parabolic long; shorts only below the 200-day, never above it unless it is a parabolic short.
facts.claim: B26: no longs below the 200-day simple moving average, except a parabolic long.

facts.quote: No chasing: never buy more than 4% above the buy point.
facts.claim: C28: never buy more than 4% above the buy point.

facts.quote: Chasing costs size, not risk: the stop stays under the buy point, so the distance grows and the shares shrink (A5).
facts.claim: C28: chasing costs size, because the stop stays put and the distance grows.

facts.quote: Too stretched to buy: skip a long that is more than 10% above its 10-day average.
facts.claim: C29: skip a long more than 10% above its 10-day average.

facts.quote: Buy leaders: an RS rating of 80 or more, in one of the strongest groups, except parabolic and mean-reversion trades.
facts.claim: C31: buy leaders, an RS rating of 80 or more in a strong group.

facts.quote: Time stop: a trade still under 1R after 10 trading days is sold, freeing the money.
facts.claim: C33: a trade still under 1R after 10 trading days is sold.

facts.quote: A climax run on your own long (Bracco's parabolic burst): sell a big part into it, a judgment call.
facts.claim: C34: sell a big part into a climax run, a judgment call.

facts.claim: C35: we swing trade; a winner can be held longer while it keeps working.

facts.claim: D41: a real stop order with the broker.

facts.claim: D42: never own more than 1% of a stock's average daily volume.

facts.quote: After the first third at 3R: another third at 5R, then trail the last third; adjustable.
facts.claim: E51: another third at 5R, then trail the last third.

facts.claim: E52: trail the 10-day for fast movers, the 21-day for steadier ones; sell on a close below it.

facts.quote: Entries are market orders.

facts.claim: F62: the stop sits a few cents under the day's low.

walkthroughs.title: UTHR, September 2025: the textbook Slingshot
steps: UTHR, September 2025. A 37.7% news gap on 2025-09-02 is the drive. Three tiny red days hug the line.

walkthroughs.title: URI, November 2016: the trims and the trail
steps: URI, November 2016. A 9.3% gap the session after the election, a 17.1% day. Three small red candles follow.

A 2.3% stop. 3R in 6 sessions: a third off, stop to breakeven. A third at 5R. The rest trails the 10-day.

questions.q: In one line, what is a Slingshot?
choices: A pullback closing over a 4-day line
A breakout over a flat base ceiling
A one-day dip under the prior low
A gap up bought on the opening bar
questions.answer: A pullback closing over a 4-day line
questions.why: A pullback in a strong stock that closes back over the 4-day EMA of the highs. Scot1and: take a powerful stock, stretch it with a pullback, enter when momentum resumes.
questions.lesson_line: A Slingshot is a strong stock catching its breath, then closing back over its 4-day line.

wrong.A breakout over a flat base ceiling: That is a base breakout. A Slingshot is a short pullback inside a run, not a box.
wrong.A one-day dip under the prior low: That is an Oops reversal, one session. A Slingshot needs closes under its line first.
wrong.A gap up bought on the opening bar: The gap is the drive that comes before. It is never the Slingshot buy.

questions.q: Tap the number that fits the blank.
questions.why: 4. The line is the 4-period EMA of the daily highs. Scot1and: my Slingshot indicator is simply a 4EMA of the highs.
questions.lesson_line: Four days, of the highs. Draw it on the chart before you look for the setup.
questions.sentence: The Slingshot's line is the ___-period EMA of the daily highs.

questions.q: The Slingshot's line is an average of the daily closes.
questions.why: False. It is the 4-period EMA of the daily HIGHS, not of closes. Analyzing Alpha: the indicator fires when the close crosses the 4-ema of the highs.
questions.lesson_line: Highs, not closes. The close is what crosses the line; the line itself is built from the highs.

questions.q: A stock gaps up 18% on earnings and closes over the 4-day EMA of highs that same day. Is that the Slingshot trigger?
choices: No; the gap day is not the trigger
Yes; the close is over the line
Yes, if volume is heavy on the gap
questions.answer: No; the gap day is not the trigger
questions.why: No. The drive day is never the trigger. The gap is the engine; the Slingshot comes later, after a pullback under the line.
questions.lesson_line: The gap is the engine. The Slingshot is the pullback after it, never the gap day itself.

wrong.Yes; the close is over the line: A close over the line on the drive day is the drive, not a trigger. Nothing has pulled back yet.
wrong.Yes, if volume is heavy on the gap: Volume does not turn a gap day into a Slingshot. The order is drive, pullback, then the close back over.

questions.q: On a Slingshot the stop goes a few cents under the drive day's low.
questions.why: False. The stop goes a few cents under the trigger day's low, as a real stop order. Scot1and: I typically place my stop at the low of the slingshot day.
questions.lesson_line: Stop first: a few cents under the trigger day's low.

questions.q: What has to happen before the pullback for a Slingshot to exist?
choices: A drive: a strong move up first
A long flat base under the highs
A close under the 200-day
A low-volume drift down to the line
questions.answer: A drive: a strong move up first
questions.why: A drive. The drive comes first: a powerful stock that recently made a strong move. A pullback in a downtrend is merely an opportunity to sell into strength.
questions.lesson_line: No drive, no Slingshot. The pullback has to have something to sling from.

wrong.A long flat base under the highs: A base is a rest, not a drive. The Slingshot wants a fresh burst of strength first.
wrong.A close under the 200-day: That is the opposite of strength. A pullback in a downtrend is a chance to sell, not to buy.
wrong.A low-volume drift down to the line: A drift down is the pullback, not the drive. The drive is the move up before it.

questions.q: We buy Slingshots in leaders: an RS rating of 80 or more, in a strong group.
questions.why: True. Buy leaders: an RS rating of 80 or more, in one of the strongest groups. Scot1and finds power with strength scans, including high RS against the S&P.
questions.lesson_line: A Slingshot in a laggard is a bounce with a name. Buy the leaders.

questions.q: Does a Slingshot trigger day need a volume surge?
choices: No; ordinary volume is the picture
Yes, at least double the average
Yes, the biggest day of the pullback
questions.answer: No; ordinary volume is the picture
questions.why: No. No volume surge is needed on the trigger day; ordinary volume is the picture. The A+ row reads: no gap, ordinary volume.
questions.lesson_line: A Slingshot is not a breakout. Do not wait for a crowd on the trigger day.

wrong.Yes, at least double the average: That is a breakout's demand. The Slingshot's trigger is a close back over the line, on ordinary volume.
wrong.Yes, the biggest day of the pullback: The pullback's quiet days are the point. The trigger needs no volume surge at all.

questions.q: The market reading is Yellow. What changes for a Slingshot you want to buy?
choices: Smaller size and fewer positions
Nothing changes; Yellow is full risk
Only A+ setups, at full size
No new longs until it turns Green
questions.why: Smaller and fewer. Green is full size; Yellow smaller and fewer; Orange only A+ setups; Red mostly cash and shorts.
questions.lesson_line: Read the market before the chart. Yellow means smaller and fewer, not none.

wrong.Nothing changes; Yellow is full risk: Full risk is Green. Yellow trims the size and the count.
wrong.Only A+ setups, at full size: That is Orange. Yellow still allows A and B setups, smaller.
wrong.No new longs until it turns Green: That is closer to Red. Yellow still buys, just smaller and fewer.

questions.q: Tap the number that fits the blank.
questions.why: 4%. Never buy more than 4% above the buy point. Chasing costs size, not risk: the stop stays put, the distance grows, the shares shrink.
questions.lesson_line: Four percent over the buy point and I am done. I would rather miss it than chase it.
questions.sentence: Never buy a Slingshot more than ___% over the buy point.

questions.q: Where does the Slingshot stop live once you are in?
choices: With the broker, as a real order
In your head, acted on at the close
As an alert on the chart, no order
questions.answer: With the broker, as a real order
questions.why: With the broker. Every position has a real stop order with the broker, not a stop kept in your head.
questions.lesson_line: A stop in your head is a debate. A stop with the broker is an appointment.

wrong.In your head, acted on at the close: A stop you watch is a stop you argue with. The rule is a real order.
wrong.As an alert on the chart, no order: An alert tells you; it does not sell. The stop order does.

questions.q: A stock above its 200-day with the 50-day and the 200-day both falling can still be a Slingshot.
questions.why: False. Both averages falling is a bounce in a downtrend, not a Slingshot. Scot1and: a pullback in a stock in a downtrend is merely an opportunity to sell into strength.
questions.lesson_line: Falling averages mean a downtrend. A Slingshot lives inside an uptrend.

questions.q: What makes the Slingshot stop tight, in Scot1and's own words?
choices: A tight range before the trigger
A heavy-volume trigger day
A stop set at the 50-day
A wide pullback, so the stop sits far
questions.answer: A tight range before the trigger
questions.why: Tight trading ranges before the trigger. They show the selling pressure waning and, more importantly, they permit very tight stops.
questions.lesson_line: Tight before the trigger means a tight stop after it. That is the whole advantage.

wrong.A heavy-volume trigger day: Volume does not set the stop's distance. The trigger day's low does, and a tight pullback keeps it close.
wrong.A stop set at the 50-day: The stop is the trigger day's low, not an average that may sit far below.
wrong.A wide pullback, so the stop sits far: The opposite. A wide pullback means a wide stop and a smaller size.

questions.q: A clean Slingshot on an $8 stock that trades $3 million a day is still ours to buy.
questions.why: False. Trade only stocks at $10 or more that trade at least $20 million a day. A clean shape in a thin stock is still a thin stock.
questions.lesson_line: Price and dollar volume come before the chart. Under the floor, we do not even watch it.

questions.q: By our card, where does a decisive Slingshot trigger day close within its range?
choices: In the top 30% of its range
Anywhere, once it is over the line
In the lower half, a shakeout
Exactly at the midpoint
questions.answer: In the top 30% of its range
questions.why: In the top 30% of its range, 0.7 or more, and it opens less than 2% over the prior close. The A+ row: closes at 78% to 99% of its range.
questions.lesson_line: Decisive means near the high of the day. A mid-range close is a shrug, not a trigger.

wrong.Anywhere, once it is over the line: Over the line is the first test. Where it closes in its range is the second.
wrong.In the lower half, a shakeout: A lower-half close is a weak day. The trigger wants buyers in charge at the bell.
wrong.Exactly at the midpoint: The midpoint is indecision. The card wants the top 30%.

questions.q: A trigger day that opens 3% over the prior close still counts as decisive on our card.
questions.why: False. A decisive trigger opens less than 2% over the prior close. Buying a trigger day that gaps up 2% or more is a named mistake.
questions.lesson_line: A gap on the trigger day is a chase in disguise. The close should come to you.

questions.q: Which pullback is orderly by our card?
choices: Inside 1.6 ATR, small red bars
One 5% red bar on heavy volume
A 3 ATR range with two gap days
questions.why: The whole pullback inside about 1.6 ATR, no red body over 3.5% of price, no down day on above-average volume. Scot1and: tight ranges before the trigger are ideal.
questions.lesson_line: An orderly pullback is small bars on quiet volume. A big red bar on volume is selling, not resting.

wrong.One 5% red bar on heavy volume: A red body over 3.5% on above-average volume breaks the orderly test twice.
wrong.A 3 ATR range with two gap days: Three ATR is nearly twice the card's range. That is choppy, like TCOM at 1.85 ATR.

questions.q: What is this day?
choices: The drive; a pullback has to come first
The Slingshot trigger; buy the close
A failed Slingshot
questions.answer: The drive; a pullback has to come first
questions.why: The drive. The drive day is never the trigger. Scot1and: take a powerful stock and stretch it with a pullback; then when momentum resumes we enter.
questions.lesson_line: Drive, pullback, resumption. The order never changes.

wrong.The Slingshot trigger; buy the close: Buying the earnings gap day as the Slingshot is a named mistake. It is never the trigger.
wrong.A failed Slingshot: Nothing has failed. Nothing has even set up yet; the pullback has not started.

questions.story: A leader reports and gaps up 24%, closing near its high. That close is also above the 4-day EMA of highs. Nothing has pulled back yet.

questions.q: You bought the trigger close at 93.86 with the stop at 91.69. What is the risk in percent?
questions.why: 2.31%. The fill minus the stop, divided by the fill. Inside the 3% a stop usually sits within. That was URI's stop, 2.3%.
questions.lesson_line: Know the risk in percent before the close prints. The stop sets the size.

questions.q: On a Slingshot winner the first trim is half at 3R, and the rest rides the trail.
questions.why: False. The hard rule is a third at 3R, another third at 5R, then trail the last third.
questions.lesson_line: A third at 3R, a third at 5R, trail the rest. Same plan as every swing setup.

questions.q: Which is it?
choices: A Slingshot
A 20 EMA pullback
A Remount
questions.why: A Slingshot. Look at which line was lost: the 4-day line, not the 20-day EMA. A 20 EMA pullback touches the 20-day, holds it, and is bought on the intraday turn.
questions.lesson_line: Name the line that was lost. The 4-day line is the Slingshot; the 20-day is the other setup.

wrong.A 20 EMA pullback: It never touched the 20-day EMA. The line lost and taken back was the 4-day line.
wrong.A Remount: A Remount takes back a slow line, the 50-day or 200-day, after weeks under it. Four sessions under a 4-day line is a Slingshot.

questions.story: The stock closed under its 4-day EMA of highs for four sessions and never touched its 20-day EMA. Then it closed back over the 4-day line.

questions.q: After entry, a Slingshot that trades under the stop is sold, and the stop is never widened.
questions.why: True. A trade under the stop ends it; no widening. The stop only moves up, never down or wider.
questions.lesson_line: My stop is my stop. Widening it is the mistake with a name.

questions.q: Tap the number that fits the blank.
questions.why: 10. A trade still under 1R after 10 trading days is sold, freeing the money.
questions.lesson_line: Ten days and nothing: sell it and free the money.
questions.sentence: A Slingshot still under 1R after ___ trading days is sold.

questions.q: Drive leg high 110.00, pullback low 101.20. How deep is the pullback, in percent?
questions.why: 8%. The drive leg's highest high minus the pullback's lowest low, divided by the high. Scot1and: the setup targets the reversal of a shallow pullback.
questions.lesson_line: Measure the depth from the drive's high. Shallow is the picture.

questions.q: The pullback's high is 68.40, its low 66.10, and the ATR is 1.50. How many ATR is the range?
questions.why: 1.53 ATR. The range divided by the ATR, inside the card's about 1.6. An orderly pullback also has no red body over 3.5% and no down day on heavy volume.
questions.lesson_line: Range over ATR. Under about 1.6 and it is resting, not unwinding.

questions.q: You bought the trigger close at 20.46 with the stop at 19.96. Where is 3R?
questions.why: 21.96. One R is the fill minus the stop; add three of those to the fill. RELY, an earnings-gap Slingshot, got there and kept stair-stepping up the 10-day.
questions.lesson_line: Know your 3R before the open. The first third comes off there.

questions.q: What now?
choices: Hold; the stop decides
Sell at the close; the reclaim failed
Widen the stop under the pullback low
Add; it is cheaper now
questions.why: Hold. A close back under the line on the next session is a warning, not an exit. The stop is the exit, and it is still below.
questions.lesson_line: A close back under the line is a warning. The stop is the decision.

wrong.Sell at the close; the reclaim failed: One close back under the line is a warning. The stop is the exit, not the line.
wrong.Widen the stop under the pullback low: The stop only moves up, never wider.
wrong.Add; it is cheaper now: Full size at one price with one stop. No adding.

questions.story: You bought the trigger close at 20.46 with the stop at 19.96. The next day closes at 20.30, back under the line, above the stop.

questions.q: Buy at the close, or pass?
choices: Pass; a gap and a weak close
Buy; the close is over the line
Buy half size
questions.answer: Pass; a gap and a weak close
questions.why: Pass. A decisive trigger opens less than 2% over the prior close and closes in the top 30% of its range. This day gapped 3% and closed mid-range.
questions.lesson_line: A gap up into a mid-range close is news, not resumption. Let it set up again.

wrong.Buy; the close is over the line: Over the line is one test. The gap and the mid-range close fail the other two.
wrong.Buy half size: Size does not fix a failed gate. A decisive trigger is a gate on our card.

questions.story: The pullback is four tight closes, 6% deep. Today opens 3% up on news and closes over the line, mid-range.

questions.q: Where is the stop now?
choices: 49.10, the first 30-minute low
Sell at the open, 49.40
No stop until it reclaims 50.00
Get out; the gap is past 2R
questions.why: 49.10. A gap through the stop hands it to the first 30-minute low. That low is inside the 2R ceiling, so it is the new stop.
questions.lesson_line: A gap through the stop is the one exception. The first 30 minutes decide.

wrong.Sell at the open, 49.40: The gap rule gives it the first 30 minutes. The open is not the decision.
wrong.No stop until it reclaims 50.00: There is always a stop. The new one is the 30-minute low.
wrong.Get out; the gap is past 2R: One R is 2.00 here, so 49.10 is inside 2R. The ceiling has not been hit.

questions.story: You bought a Slingshot close at 52.00 with the stop at 50.00. It gaps open at 49.40. The first 30-minute bar's low is 49.10.

questions.q: Buy it?
choices: No; a new run under the line first
Yes; the trigger fired again
Yes, with a wider stop this time
questions.answer: No; a new run under the line first
questions.why: No. Re-entry only on a new Slingshot. That means a new run of at least 3 closes under the line, then a new close over it. Its own stop too.
questions.lesson_line: A stop-out is not a verdict on the setup. A new Slingshot is a new pullback first.

wrong.Yes; the trigger fired again: Re-buying the same pullback again and again is a named mistake. The pullback has to form again first.
wrong.Yes, with a wider stop this time: A wider stop to avoid a repeat is the mistake, not the fix. And the setup has not formed again.

questions.story: Your Slingshot stopped out the day after the trigger. Two sessions later price closes back over the line again.

questions.q: A Slingshot trigger more than 10% above its 10-day average is skipped as too stretched.
questions.why: True. Skip a long that is more than 10% above its 10-day average. It rarely binds on a Slingshot, but it can after an explosive gap with a shallow pullback.
questions.lesson_line: A stretched trigger is a chase with a different name.

questions.q: Take the close?
choices: No; the report is inside 3 sessions
Yes; the trigger is decisive
Yes; a huge drive protects it
questions.answer: No; the report is inside 3 sessions
questions.why: No. No new buys in the 3 days before a report. FSLR's reversal the next session was the earnings reaction, not a setup failure.
questions.lesson_line: A rally Slingshot near a report is the case that binds. Wait for the report.

wrong.Yes; the trigger is decisive: The trigger is fine and the calendar still says no. The earnings rule is a hard line.
wrong.Yes; a huge drive protects it: A giant drive does not make the trigger safer. The next session was the earnings reaction.

questions.story: The drive was a 45.5% day. The pullback is 3 closes and 7.1% deep, and the trigger closed at 0.94 of its range. The report lands tomorrow.

questions.q: A Slingshot is bought at one price with one stop, full size; adding later on a 50-day reclaim is not our play.
questions.why: True. The full size at one price with one stop; no adding. The add on the 50-day reclaim is not taught.
questions.lesson_line: One price, one stop, full size. Adds are a different trade.

questions.q: On a Slingshot the stop moves to breakeven as soon as the trade is 1R up.
questions.why: False. Breakeven once the trade is 2R up; anywhere from 2R to 5R is allowed. The first trim at 3R is the natural moment.
questions.lesson_line: Breakeven somewhere from 2R to 5R. The first trim at 3R is the natural moment.

questions.q: What did the stop do?
choices: Its job: a planned loss of 1R
Cost you the trade; it needed room
Nothing; the pullback low was the exit
questions.answer: Its job: a planned loss of 1R
questions.why: Its job. The next session traded through the trigger day's low, which is what the stop under it is placed to detect. The 3R level printed 4 sessions later without us; a second try needs a new run of closes under the line.
questions.lesson_line: A loss taken at plan is the system working. The next try is a new Slingshot.

wrong.Cost you the trade; it needed room: Room is a wider loss, not a better trade. The edge is in the resumption, and this one did not resume on time.
wrong.Nothing; the pullback low was the exit: The stop is the trigger day's low, not the pullback low. The pullback low was broken too.

questions.story: Drive +8.2% on volume, three closes under the line, 6.6% deep. The trigger closed at 0.94 of its range; you bought 122.76, stop 119.10. The next session opens 121.51 and falls to 115.90.

questions.q: Your move?
choices: No new longs; mostly cash, shorts
Buy; the chart beats the reading
Buy small, stop under the low
questions.answer: No new longs; mostly cash, shorts
questions.why: No new longs. Red is mostly cash, plus shorts below the 200-day. The best Slingshot in a Red market is a chart to study, not a buy.
questions.lesson_line: The reading comes before the chart. Red means sit on your hands.

wrong.Buy; the chart beats the reading: Orange still allows A+ setups. Red allows mostly cash and shorts.
wrong.Buy small, stop under the low: Red is mostly cash and shorts. A small long still goes against the guide.

questions.story: The reading turned Red last week. Today a leader closes decisively back over its 4-day line after a quiet pullback.

questions.q: The last third of a Slingshot winner trails which line?
choices: 10-day if fast, 21-day if steadier
The 4-day line, on any close under
The 50-day, on a touch
No trail; sell it all at 5R
questions.why: The 10-day for a fast mover, the 21-day for a steadier one, sold on a close below. Scot1and trails on the 4-day line itself; that is his, not ours.
questions.lesson_line: Trail the rising average. Sell the close below it, not the touch.

wrong.The 4-day line, on any close under: That is Scot1and's own trail, a close under the EMA 4. Our default is the 10-day or the 21-day.
wrong.The 50-day, on a touch: The 50-day is too far for a fast mover, and a touch is not a close below.
wrong.No trail; sell it all at 5R: 5R is the second third, not the exit. The last third rides the trail.

questions.q: What is the lesson?
choices: Prefer a rising 50-day over the 200-day
Never buy a three-close pullback
Too tight; the pullback low was the stop
questions.why: Prefer the 50-day over the 200-day and rising. Here the 50-day sat under the 200-day, the location our card prefers to avoid. The stop was the rule's stop and the loss was planned.
questions.lesson_line: Location matters. Prefer a Slingshot over a rising 50-day that sits above the 200-day.

wrong.Never buy a three-close pullback: Three closes is the minimum, not a flaw. The location was the problem here.
wrong.Too tight; the pullback low was the stop: The stop is a few cents under the trigger day's low. The stock fell 12.6% under the buy within 20 sessions; a wider stop would have lost more.

questions.story: Drive +8.8% on volume, three closes under the line, 6.9% deep, the trigger closed at its high. You bought 24.90, stop 24.53. On the trigger day the 50-day sat under the 200-day. Stopped the next session.

questions.q: Take the close or pass?
choices: Pass; an indecisive close
Take it; the close is over the line
Take it; the pullback was tidy
questions.why: Pass. A decisive trigger closes in the top 30% of its range, 0.7 or more. At 0.54 it is the middle of the bar; that one stopped at 0R.
questions.lesson_line: The first close over the line is not enough. It has to close like it means it.

wrong.Take it; the close is over the line: Over the line and mid-range is a shrug. The card wants 0.7 or more.
wrong.Take it; the pullback was tidy: The pullback passes and the trigger fails. Every gate has to pass.

questions.story: A drive, then a tidy pullback. Today the first close back over the line lands at 0.54 of the day's range, the middle of the bar.

questions.q: Account 40,000. Risk 0.75%. Fill 269.73, stop 259.09. How many shares?
questions.why: 28. Account times risk percent, divided by the fill minus the stop, rounded down. The stop sets the size, never the other way round. That was MELI's trade.
questions.lesson_line: Stop first, distance second, size last.

questions.q: Our card's wider stop choice for a Slingshot sits where?
choices: Under the lower of two days' lows
Under the pullback low, always
Under the 50-day average
A full ATR under the trigger low
questions.answer: Under the lower of two days' lows
questions.why: A few cents under the lower of the trigger day's and the prior day's lows. Never wider than the bottom of the pullback; Scot1and: at most, the bottom of the consolidation period.
questions.lesson_line: Wider means the prior day's low at most. The pullback's bottom is the limit, never a rule.

wrong.Under the pullback low, always: The pullback's bottom is the limit of the wider choice, not the default.
wrong.Under the 50-day average: An average is not a low. The stop is a few cents under a day's low.
wrong.A full ATR under the trigger low: An ATR is a distance, not a level. The stop sits a few cents under a low.

questions.q: If a Slingshot winner turns into a climax run, we sell a big part into it.
questions.why: True. A climax run on your own long, Bracco's parabolic burst: sell a big part into it, a judgment call.
questions.lesson_line: Sell into a climax. Nobody rings a bell at the top, but the burst is the bell.

questions.q: A Slingshot that gaps open past 3R has its first third sold at the close, not at the open.
questions.why: False. If a stock opens above a trim level, take that trim at the open.
questions.lesson_line: A gap through a trim level is the trim. Take it at the open.

questions.q: Which rule is this loss the case for?
choices: Buy leaders: RS 80 or more, strong group
Never buy a three-close pullback
Widen the stop past the pullback low
questions.answer: Buy leaders: RS 80 or more, strong group
questions.why: Buy leaders. The bars cannot say whether this stock was a leader by RS that day; the rule exists for that case. The stop did its job.
questions.lesson_line: Two stocks, one drive day, one chart shape. The leader is the one to own.

wrong.Never buy a three-close pullback: Three closes is the minimum and the winner on the same drive day had three too.
wrong.Widen the stop past the pullback low: The low 20 sessions later was 10% under the buy. A wider stop loses more, not less.

questions.story: Same market-wide drive day as a winner. Three closes under the line, 5.5% deep, a 0.76 close. You bought 70.86, stop 68.12. Stopped on day 2.

questions.q: Was the second try allowed?
choices: Yes; a new trigger with its own stop
No; one try per drive
No; the first stop-out ends the stock
questions.answer: Yes; a new trigger with its own stop
questions.why: Yes. Re-entry only on a new Slingshot with its own stop, at most 3 tries a week. The second try was stopped on day 4; a first failure warns the pullback was no longer orderly.
questions.lesson_line: A second try is a new trade with every rule. The first failure is a warning you carry into it.

wrong.No; one try per drive: The limit is 3 tries in a week and 6 in a month, not one per drive.
wrong.No; the first stop-out ends the stock: A stop-out ends the trade. A new run of closes under the line and a new close over it is a new setup.

questions.story: An earnings gap of 29.5%. A first Slingshot six sessions earlier stopped out. Now a new run of three closes under the line and a close over it. You bought 185.93, stop 177.98; it reached 0.31R, then gapped under the stop on day 4.

questions.q: The stock trades 1,500,000 shares a day on average. The most shares we may own?
questions.why: 15,000. Never own more than 1% of a stock's average daily volume.
questions.lesson_line: One percent of the daily volume, and not a share more.

questions.q: Slingshot?
choices: No; a bounce in a downtrend
Yes; above the 200-day is enough
Yes; the drive makes it ours
questions.answer: No; a bounce in a downtrend
questions.why: No. With the 50-day and the 200-day both falling it is a bounce in a downtrend, not a Slingshot. Scot1and: a pullback in a downtrend is an opportunity to sell into strength.
questions.lesson_line: Above the 200-day is not enough when both lines point down. Trend first, then the pullback.

wrong.Yes; above the 200-day is enough: Above the line with both averages falling is a bounce. Our card calls it a downtrend.
wrong.Yes; the drive makes it ours: A drive inside a downtrend is a rally to sell into, in Scot1and's own words.

questions.story: The close is above the 200-day. The 50-day has been falling for weeks, and the 200-day too. A drive, three closes under the line, now a close back over it.

questions.q: Which is it?
choices: A Remount
A Slingshot
An Oops reversal
questions.why: A Remount. Count the closes under the line and name the line. It lost a slow line, the 50-day, for weeks and took it back. A Slingshot slips under the 4-day EMA of highs for a few sessions.
questions.lesson_line: Count the closes and name the line. Weeks under a slow line is a Remount.

wrong.A Slingshot: The line is wrong and the count is long. A Slingshot's line is the 4-day EMA of highs, lost for a few sessions.
wrong.An Oops reversal: An Oops is one day: open under the prior close, reclaim it the same session. This took weeks.

questions.story: The stock closed under its 50-day for eleven sessions. Then it closed back over it on volume.

questions.q: Which is it?
choices: An Oops reversal, one session
A Slingshot off the 4-day line
A Remount over a slow line
questions.why: An Oops: one day. It opens under the prior close, trades under the prior low and reclaims the close the same session. A Slingshot needs at least three closes under its line first.
questions.lesson_line: One session is an Oops. A Slingshot needs days under the line before the close back over.

wrong.A Slingshot off the 4-day line: No run of closes under the 4-day line came first. One session cannot be a Slingshot.
wrong.A Remount over a slow line: A Remount takes back a slow line after weeks under it. This is one day around the prior close.

questions.story: It opened under the prior close and traded under the prior day's low. Then it closed back over the prior close, all in one session.

questions.q: A Slingshot trigger on ordinary volume is graded down for the lack of a surge.
questions.why: False. No volume surge is needed; ordinary volume is the picture. The A+ row reads: no gap, ordinary volume.
questions.lesson_line: Ordinary volume on the trigger is the textbook, not a flaw.

questions.q: Buy now?
choices: No; wait for the close over the line
Yes; the first red day is the entry
Yes; add on the 50-day reclaim later
questions.answer: No; wait for the close over the line
questions.why: No. Buying the first red day of the pullback instead of waiting for the close back over the line is a named mistake. Scot1and: then when momentum resumes we enter.
questions.lesson_line: Feeling it coming is not a trigger. The close back over the line is.

wrong.Yes; the first red day is the entry: The first red day is the start of the pullback, not its end. Momentum has not resumed.
wrong.Yes; add on the 50-day reclaim later: No adding; one price, one stop. And there is no entry yet to add to.

questions.story: The drive was an earnings gap. Day one of the pullback is a small red bar closing under the 4-day line. You feel it coming.

questions.q: What happens to the last third?
choices: Hold until a close under the trail
Sell; two months is long enough
Sell on the first red day
questions.answer: Hold until a close under the trail
questions.why: Hold it. The last third trails the 10-day for a fast mover, sold on a close below. A winner can be held longer while it keeps working; GRMN was 50% higher in two months.
questions.lesson_line: Two thirds banked, the last third on the trail. Time is not a reason to sell a working trade.

wrong.Sell; two months is long enough: We swing trade, and a winner can be held longer while it keeps working. The trail decides, not the calendar.
wrong.Sell on the first red day: A red day above the trail line is noise. The exit is a close below the line.

questions.story: You bought the trigger close at 66.08, stop 64.04. You trimmed at 3R and 5R. Two months on the stock is 50% higher and still above its 10-day.

questions.q: Chris Moody's two-average SlingShot System on TradingView is the same setup as ours.
questions.why: False. Drawing the wrong line is a named mistake: a 4-day EMA of closes, or Chris Moody's two-average system. Ours is the 4-period EMA of the daily highs.
questions.lesson_line: Same name, different line. Ours is one line: the 4-day EMA of the highs.

questions.q: Hidden ticker, the day it closes back over its 4-day line after a news gap. Take the close or pass?
choices: Take it; a decisive close after the rest
Pass; the gap day was the trigger
Pass; three red days is too long
questions.answer: Take it; a decisive close after the rest
questions.why: Take it. A huge news gap, then three tiny red days hugging the line. Then a decisive close back over it at 0.92 of its range. It reached 3R in 3 sessions.
questions.lesson_line: Drive, tiny red days, a decisive close. That is the whole picture.

wrong.Pass; the gap day was the trigger: The gap day is the drive, never the trigger. The trigger is today's close back over the line.
wrong.Pass; three red days is too long: Three closes under the line is the minimum, not too long.

questions.q: Hidden ticker, the first day it closes back over its 4-day line after a pullback. Take the close or pass?
choices: Pass; the close sits mid-range
Take it; the close is over the line
Take it; the pullback was short
questions.why: Pass. The first close back over the line landed at 0.54 of its range, the middle of the bar. A decisive trigger closes at 0.7 or more. It stopped at 0R.
questions.lesson_line: Look at where the trigger day closed in its own range before you look at the line.

wrong.Take it; the close is over the line: Over the line is the first test. A mid-range close fails the second.
wrong.Take it; the pullback was short: The pullback is fine. The trigger day is the problem.

questions.q: On one stock we make at most 3 Slingshot tries in a week and 6 in a month.
questions.why: True. The same stock: at most 3 tries in a week and 6 in a month. Each is a new Slingshot with its own stop.
questions.lesson_line: Three tries a week, six a month. After that the stock has told you something.

questions.q: What now?
choices: Sell; hold through only if up 5R
Hold; the trend is up, so it is fine
Sell half and hold the rest
questions.answer: Sell; hold through only if up 5R
questions.why: Sell. We hold through a report only if the trade is up 5R. A rally Slingshot near a report is the case that binds; a PEG Slingshot is usually weeks from the next one.
questions.lesson_line: Earnings is a gap you cannot stop. Five R buys the ticket; 1.5R does not.

wrong.Hold; the trend is up, so it is fine: The trend does not report earnings. The gap does, and 1.5R is no cushion.
wrong.Sell half and hold the rest: Half of a 1.5R cushion is still under the 5R line.

questions.story: Your rally Slingshot is up 1.5R. The report comes after the close in two sessions.

questions.q: You bought the trigger close at 13.94, stop 13.42. It trades to 15.50. How many R is that?
questions.why: 3R. The gain divided by the fill minus the stop. That is where the first third comes off; FRO got there in 7 sessions.
questions.lesson_line: Count in R, not dollars. 3R is the first trim.

questions.q: Which grades higher?
choices: The one over a rising 50 above the 200
Equal; the line is what matters
The flat one; it is less stretched
questions.answer: The one over a rising 50 above the 200
questions.why: The one over a rising 50-day that sits above the 200-day. Our card prefers that location; the other is the location it prefers to avoid.
questions.lesson_line: Same shape, two locations. Rising averages in the right order earn the better grade.

wrong.Equal; the line is what matters: The line is the trigger. Location grades the trade, and the grade sets the size.
wrong.The flat one; it is less stretched: Less stretched is not a grade. A 50-day under the 200-day is the location we prefer to avoid.

questions.story: Two Slingshots with the same drive and the same tidy pullback. One sits over a rising 50-day above the 200-day. The other sits over a flat 50-day that is under the 200-day.

questions.q: What do you do?
choices: Sell; under 1R after 10 days
Hold; the stop has not hit
Add; it is still above the line
questions.why: Sell. A trade still under 1R after 10 trading days is sold, freeing the money. A Slingshot is a resumption, and this one has not resumed.
questions.lesson_line: Ten days and nothing. The money has somewhere better to be.

wrong.Hold; the stop has not hit: The stop is one exit. The time stop is another, and it fired.
wrong.Add; it is still above the line: No adding. And a trade that has done nothing in 10 days is not asking for more money.

questions.story: Ten trading days after a Slingshot buy the trade sits at 0.6R, drifting sideways. The stop has not been touched.

questions.q: Three of our four rule-following Slingshot losses were stopped within two sessions, the stop doing its job.
questions.why: True. Three of the four were stopped within two sessions. The trigger day's low did not hold, which is what the stop under it is placed to detect.
questions.lesson_line: A Slingshot that fails usually fails fast. The tight stop is what makes that cheap.

questions.q: Grade?
choices: Not orderly; pass
A+; the drive is huge
B; buy half
questions.why: Pass. Orderly means the whole pullback inside about 1.6 ATR, no red body over 3.5%, no down day on above-average volume. This one is choppy; TCOM at 1.85 ATR was left out of the gallery.
questions.lesson_line: A big drive does not excuse a messy pullback. Orderly is a gate.

wrong.A+; the drive is huge: The drive is one row of the grade. The pullback fails the orderly test on every count.
wrong.B; buy half: Half of a messy pullback is still a messy pullback. Orderly is a gate, not a grade.

questions.story: A drive, then a pullback whose bars swing 1.85 ATR high to low, with one 4% red bar on heavy volume. Today it closes over the line.

questions.q: Size?
choices: Sized down
Normal size
Sized up
questions.why: Sized down. A and B setups at normal size; A+ sized up; B- or lower sized down. Risk by grade puts B- at 0.25% to 0.5%.
questions.lesson_line: The grade sets the size. A B- gets the smallest risk, or no trade at all.

wrong.Normal size: Normal size is for A and B setups. B- is sized down.

questions.story: Every gate passes, but on your read this Slingshot grades B-. The reading is Green.

questions.q: You buy the trigger close. Entry, stop and first trim?
choices: 93.86; stop 91.69; a third at 3R
93.86; stop 88.20; out at 2R
93.86; stop at the gap low; hold to 5R
questions.why: Market at the close, 93.86; the stop a few cents under the day's low, 91.69; a third at 3R. URI reached 3R in 6 sessions and the trend ran two months.
questions.lesson_line: Entry, stop, trim, trail. Write it before the close prints; execute it without a debate.

wrong.93.86; stop 88.20; out at 2R: A stop down at 88.20 is nowhere near the day's low, and 2R is breakeven's floor, not the trim.
wrong.93.86; stop at the gap low; hold to 5R: The gap low is the drive's start, far below. And the first third comes off at 3R, not 5R.

questions.story: URI, November 2016: a 17.1% drive on a 9.3% gap, then three small red candles. Today it closes at 0.88 of its range, back over the line at 93.86. The day's low was a few cents over 91.69.

questions.q: Slingshot?
choices: No; no drive to sling from
Yes; the shape is the setup
Yes; the close is decisive
questions.answer: No; no drive to sling from
questions.why: No. By our current default, the drive is a gap or a strong rally, and this climb has neither. The drive comes first; Scot1and takes a powerful stock that recently made a strong move. This one reached 4.1R anyway, which the test cannot credit to the setup.
questions.lesson_line: The shape without the drive is a pullback, not a Slingshot. The engine comes first.

wrong.Yes; the shape is the setup: The shape is half the setup. The drive is the other half, and it is missing.
wrong.Yes; the close is decisive: A decisive close is only the trigger. The drive has to come first.

questions.story: A steady climber: no gap, no 4% volume day, no 20% in five sessions in the 25 sessions before. Four closes under the 4-day line, then a decisive close over it.

questions.q: The only time a Slingshot stop moves against you is the gap rule: the first 30-minute low on a gap-down day.
questions.why: True. The stop only moves up, never down or wider. The one exception is the gap rule: the low of the first 30-minute bar is the new stop.
questions.lesson_line: One exception, and it is not yours to choose. The gap decides, in 30 minutes.

questions.q: What do you do?
choices: Nothing; no setup, no trade
Buy the near one; Green is full risk
Buy it small
questions.why: Nothing. No setup, no trade; cash is a position. A mid-range close is not a decisive trigger, and a near-miss is a miss.
questions.lesson_line: Green is permission, not an order. Wait for the one that passes every gate.

wrong.Buy it small: Small is a size, not a setup. Never force a trade to have something on.
wrong.Buy the near one; Green is full risk: Green sets the size for a setup that passes. It does not create one.

questions.story: Earnings season, and the reading is Green. Your list shows no Slingshot that passes every gate. One is close, but its trigger closed mid-range.

questions.q: You bought the trigger close at 66.08 with the stop at 64.04. Where is 5R?
questions.why: 76.28. One R is the fill minus the stop; add five of those to the fill. The second third comes off there.
questions.lesson_line: Know your 5R before the open. The second third comes off there.

questions.q: What comes off now?
choices: Another 30; trail the last 30
Another 45; trail the last 15
The last 60 shares, all of it
Nothing; wait for the 21-day
questions.why: Another 30, a third of the position. The first third came off at 3R, the second comes off at 5R, and you trail the last third.
questions.lesson_line: A third at 3R, a third at 5R, then trail the rest.

wrong.Another 45; trail the last 15: A third of 90 is 30, not 45. The last third, 30 shares, trails.
wrong.The last 60 shares, all of it: The plan keeps the last third on the trail, not out at 5R.
wrong.Nothing; wait for the 21-day: The trail starts after both trims. At 5R the second third comes off.

questions.story: You bought 90 shares of a Slingshot at the trigger close. You sold 30 at 3R. Today the stock reaches 5R.
